quote: In situ hybridization and immunohistochemistry revealed that NF-HEV mRNA and protein are expressed at high levels and rather selectively by HEVECs in human tonsils, Peyers's patches, and lymph nodes.
summary: Cloning paper showing the IL-33 precursor (NF-HEV) is a nuclear factor highly expressed in high endothelial venules of human lymphoid tissues; no UC data.

quote: Murine IL-33 is also cleaved by mast cell tryptase, and a tryptase inhibitor reduced IL-33-dependent allergic airway inflammation in vivo.
summary: Mast cell proteases cleave IL-33 into highly active forms that expand ILC2s and eosinophils in mice, and blocking cleavage reduced allergic airway inflammation; not a colitis study.

quote: IL-33 plays important roles in type-2 innate immunity via activation of allergic inflammation-related eosinophils, basophils, mast cells, macrophages, and group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) through its receptor ST2.
summary: Review of IL-33 in allergic inflammation and therapeutic approaches targeting the IL-33/ST2 axis; no UC-specific content.

quote: Using Il33(Cit/Cit) mice (IL-33-deficient), we establish a role for IL-33 early in the initiation of type-2 responses and the induction of nuocytes (ILC2).
summary: IL-33-deficient reporter mice show IL-33 is needed early for type-2 allergic lung responses and ILC2 induction; the work is in asthma, not colitis.

quote: Here, we have shown that Il33-deficient mice are highly susceptible to colitis and CAC.
summary: Il33-deficient mice develop dysbiosis, low IgA and IL-1alpha-driven colitis and colitis-associated cancer, so IL-33 protects the gut and inhibition may harm.

quote: Genetic perturbation of IL-33 or its receptor ST2 led to microglial dystrophy, impaired synaptic function, and behavioral abnormalities.
summary: Loss of IL-33 or ST2 impairs microglial metabolism, synapses and behaviour in developing mouse brain; no intestinal or colitis outcome.

quote: Enhanced expression of these genes induced Bach2(-/-) naive T cells to migrate toward CCR4-ligand and respond to IL33.
summary: IL33 is mentioned only as a stimulus to which Bach2-deficient naive T cells respond via ST2; no IL-33-specific finding.

quote: IL25 and IL33 are key cytokines that support ILC2s; however, mice deficient in these pathways retain some functional ILC2s.
summary: IL33 is mentioned as background for ILC2 support in a paper focused on TL1A and DR3; no IL-33 experiment.

quote: Conversely, GVHD lethality and tumor necrosis factor-α production was significantly reduced in il33(-/-) recipients.
summary: IL-33 from non-hematopoietic cells worsens acute graft-versus-host disease, including gut damage; IL-33 deletion or ST2-Fc blockade reduced lethality in mice.

quote: IL33(tm1/+) mice succumb to lethal inflammation characterized by eosinophil-dominated immune cell infiltration of multiple organs.
summary: Removing the IL-33 nuclear localization signal makes IL-33 leak out and causes ST2-dependent lethal inflammation in mice, showing excess released IL-33 drives inflammation.

quote: In mice, Il33 deficiency severely attenuates inflammation- and LTβR-activation-induced TLSs in models of colitis and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC).
summary: IL-33 is needed for tertiary lymphoid structure formation in mouse colitis and pancreatic cancer models; whether this helps or harms colitis is not stated.

quote: BackgroundGenome-wide association studies (GWASs) of asthma have consistently implicated the ORM1-like 3 and gasdermin B (ORMDL3-GSDMB), IL33, IL-1 receptor-like 1 and IL-18 receptor 1 (IL1RL1-IL18R1), RAD50-IL13, thymic stromal lymphopoietin and WD repeat domain 36 region (TSLP-WDR36), and HLA-DR/DQ regions.
summary: IL33 is named only as a previously reported asthma GWAS locus; the new findings concern TNIP1, IL13, HLA-DRA and GSDMB.

quote: However, 13 loci, including KCNK1, FBXO38, UHRF2, IL33, RUNX2, TRPS1, CAMTA1, and VAMP3, provided suggestive evidence (p < 5 × 10(-6)) of association.
summary: IL33 is one of 13 loci with suggestive association with periodontal pathogen colonization; unrelated to UC.

quote: Without this attenuating IL-33 response, females generate an encephalitogenic Th17-dominant response, which can be reversed by IL-33 treatment.
summary: Male-specific IL-33 induces ILC2s and a Th2 response that limit EAE, and IL-33 treatment reverses female susceptibility; this is a neuroinflammation model.

quote: In the stomach, IL33-treated mice developed transmural inflammation and mucous metaplasia that was mediated by Th2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 signaling.
summary: Chronic recombinant IL33 given to mice caused gastric inflammation and mucous metaplasia through Th2 signalling; stomach study, not colitis.

quote: Accordingly diarrhoea and DSS-induced colon inflammation were impaired in ST2(-/-) BALB/c mice and exacerbated in wild-type mice by treatment with exogenous recombinant IL-33, associated respectively with reduced and enhanced expression of chemokines (CXCL9 and CXCL10), and inflammatory (IL-4, IL-13, IL-1, IL-6, IL-17) and angiogenic (vascular endothelial growth factor) cytokines in vivo.
summary: In DSS colitis, IL33 and ST2 are induced early, ST2 loss reduces colitis and recombinant IL-33 worsens it via IL-4, so IL-33 signalling is pathogenic.

quote: MUC5B, REG3A, DEFA5, and IL33 might be considered as colorectal cancer [CRC] risk factors following UC in males.
summary: IL33 is one of 1480 differentially expressed genes in treatment-naive UC biopsies and is named among possible CRC risk genes in males; no specific analysis.

quote: ST2-deficient mice developed exacerbated EAU compared with WT mice, and administration of IL-33 to WT mice significantly reduced EAU severity.
summary: IL-33/ST2 signalling restrains experimental autoimmune uveitis in mice, as ST2 loss worsens disease and IL-33 treatment reduces it; not an intestinal model.

quote: Interestingly, IL33 blockade did not affect bone marrow-derived expansion and local infiltration of eosinophils, but markedly decreased M2 macrophages and SPEM features, while eosinophil depletion caused a significant reduction in both local IL33-producing M2 macrophages and SPEM in SAMP.
summary: IL33 blockade reduced M2 macrophages and metaplasia in gastritis-prone mice and recombinant IL33 induced metaplasia, so IL33 is pathogenic in gastric metaplasia; not colitis.

quote: In the present study, SureSelectXT Methyl-Seq was performed on cancerous and normal colon tissues and CLDN1, INHBA and SLC30A10 were found as candidate methylated genes.
summary: INHBA is one of three candidate methylated genes in a colorectal cancer methylation screen; the validated marker is not clearly attributed to INHBA.

quote: Survival analysis revealed that INHBA, FNBP1, PDE9A, HIST1H2BG, and CADM3 were significantly correlated with prognosis in CRC patients.
summary: Machine learning on TCGA and GEO data identified INHBA among five genes correlated with prognosis in colorectal cancer; no UC data.

quote: Further observations from bulk and single-cell RNAseq analyses indicated that TREM1 expression was significantly enriched in polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells (PMN-MDSCs) and M2-like macrophages, and correlated with downstream transcriptional targets of TREM-1 (IL8, IL-1B, IL6, MCP-1, SPP1, IL1RL, INHBA) which have been previously associated with pro-tumorigenic and immunosuppressive functions.
summary: INHBA is listed only as a TREM-1 downstream target gene in a breast cancer study.

quote: Taken together, our data indicate that CCR2 and activin A promote fibrosis during testicular inflammation by regulating macrophage function.
summary: Activin A (INHBA-encoded) and CCR2 drive macrophage-mediated testicular fibrosis in mouse orchitis, and the activin A antagonist follistatin reduced damage; not an intestinal model.

quote: In conclusion, INHBA was considered as a senescence-related regulator and a prognostic predictor in CRC, which also mediating immune evasion.
summary: INHBA was identified as a senescence-related prognostic predictor co-expressed with T-cell markers and immune checkpoints in colorectal cancer; no UC data.

quote: Finally, the gene expression of transforming growth factor β1 (Tgfb1), and smooth muscle actin (Acta2) were decreased in the irradiated skin and Acta2 and inhibin βA subunit (Inhba) were decreased in the irradiated muscle of the follistatin treated mice.
summary: Inhba expression fell in irradiated muscle of follistatin-treated mice as one readout of reduced radiation fibrosis; not an intestinal study.
